I'm ready to propose the next steps. If the structure gets approval, I’ll draft the memo and Q&A responses within 12 hours. I’ll mark any arguments as AGGRESSIVE if they rely on favorable interpretations.

1) Cross‑jurisdiction memo structure (headings + short note): I. Executive summary (objective, launch timing, ask to regulators); II. Factual background (product mechanics from TermSheet_v2, digital‑asset elements, target client segments, distribution map); III. Settled regulatory expectations (by Market A/B/C: suitability/disclosure, registration/filing, marketing controls, client categorisation rules); IV. Risk‑to‑launch table (what will materially delay/derail + mitigation owner); VII. Recommendations & next steps (preparation for optional engagement with Market A).  
2) Regulator‑facing Q&A framing (high level): Complexity — lead with layered, plain‑language disclosures and why product is targeted only at defined client segments plus sales gating and suitability scripts; Digital‑asset exposure — state precise exposure magnitude, custody/segregation model, valuation/fallback rules, concentration caps and stress‑test results; Cross‑border distribution — explain booking entity model, contractual obligations on platform/IFA partners, geofencing/technical controls, reporting/complaint handling and liability allocation; Close with proportionality rationale (controls calibrated to client sophistication) and offer targeted follow‑up data rather than broad pre‑meeting.

1) Regulatory posture — Market A: high supervisory scrutiny on crypto‑linked yield products requiring clear prominence of digital‑asset risks, tight suitability and distributor controls; Market B: broadly similar expectations but less interventionist so far; Market C: professional/institutional only routing reduces retail risk and supervisory attention.  
2) Top residual risks (with categorisation): (a) marketing/suitability enforcement in Market A if digital‑asset risk is perceived as under‑emphasised (Settled expectation); (b) Platform A being treated as a local distributor or failing to enforce geo‑blocking/onboarding, causing cross‑border distribution breaches (Uncertain / assumption‑sensitive); (c) our reliance on a 20% “benchmark” enforced via eligibility/warnings rather than a real‑time hard stop — defensible but AGGRESSIVE if regulator demands guaranteed real‑time limits; (d) custody/valuation and fallback ambiguity for tokenised exposures (Uncertain).  
3) Conditions to attach to a “go” decision: Platform A executes the redlined distribution terms (onboarding attestations, geo‑blocking, logging/reporting); front‑end eligibility gating, one‑page plain‑language risk/suitability summary and RM suitability scripts deployed; monthly portfolio snapshots, defined stress‑test cadence, and complaint/escalation reporting; documented confirmation of projected client mix/volumes and unchanged valuation/fallback mechanics.

5) Recommendation: ExCo should approve launch “go” subject to the conditions above, delegate authority to Legal/COO to withhold go‑live if key contractual/assumption items are unmet, and require a post‑launch compliance report (first 30 days) to confirm assumptions and trigger remediation if breaches arise.
